provenance: Hand-authored synthetic retrieval stress cases. Not production incidents, independently collected user data, or a claim of real-world accuracy. Captured runtime faults are provided separately by tools/generate-fixtures.py.
splitPolicy: Use calibration only to select thresholds and hard-negative rules, then freeze configuration before scoring heldOut. Report any subsequent reuse of heldOut as development data; do not present it as unseen after tuning.
scope: Three authored synthetic memories and authored synthetic language variants; no production logs, root-cause verification, human-user study, or developer-time-saved measurement.

model.name: all-MiniLM-L6-v2
model.evaluatedRuntime: Node.js native ONNX Runtime CPU (not browser WebAssembly)

corpus.embeddingInput: normalizeFailure(incident.symptom); excludes title, fix, and evidence

configuration.selectionRule: Use calibration only. Require zero accepted wrong or novel matches; maximize correctly accepted known cases; ties prefer higher minimum score, then higher margin. No held-out labels or scores participate.

metrics.note: Top-k ranks are measured before abstention. Top-3 is weak evidence with only three memory candidates. Precision is null when there are no accepted candidates.

timings.startupNote: First call in this process includes model initialization and embedding three memories. Existing disk cache may avoid downloads. Not a browser cold-start or first-network-download measurement.
timings.workload: One sequential batch-of-one inference and ranking against three pre-embedded memories per held-out query; model already initialized; the evaluator issues no concurrent inference requests, but other host load is uncontrolled.

limitations: Authored synthetic cases and a three-memory corpus are not evidence of production accuracy or saved developer time.
Calibration and held-out cases share the same three authored failure families; this is a language-variant stress test, not an independently sampled distribution.
The calibration set is tiny; zero observed false matches does not establish a low real-world false-match rate.
Cosine similarity is not a probability, confidence, or root-cause proof. Every accepted result is only a human-review candidate.
Top-3 retrieval is nearly trivial because the corpus contains only three incidents.
Tokenization truncates to 256 tokens; long reports can lose causal information. This benchmark uses short individual symptoms.
Node CPU timings do not establish browser performance, offline readiness, or cross-device performance.
Retrieval queries are individual symptom strings. This is not an end-to-end evaluation of JUnit type/message/detail assembly or a full CI triage workflow.

securityTests.scope: XML malformed/DTD/entity/byte-depth-field-count rejection; diagnostic-value preservation; memory import validation; inert text preservation; invalid embeddings; ambiguity abstention; no command execution.
securityTests.limitations: These deterministic Node tests do not execute the browser DOM. Imported markup remains literal data, so UI output escaping must also be verified in the browser. Common-secret redaction is best effort, not a security guarantee.
